modelName: A refugee student's first school year — a network of nested systems
modelNote: The worked example from Section 8 of the RCN Design Record. One student lives in five systems at once, and each of those systems sits inside a larger one (the nesting). No single system can hold the whole first-year scenario, so a Solution ME forms across them (the network). The dashed grey arrows are the coordination that exists today, taken from Spokane linkage map #7 (School-Refugee Transition: Schools, World Relief, CHW Network, Family & Individual, with SHARE_CLIENT, PRESENTS_TO and REQUEST_COORD edges). The dotted green arrows are where the ME draws its participants from. Built 2026-09-11 by Marc Pierson and Claude for the Section 8 rewrite. PROVENANCE: illustrative. Every arrow is asserted from the Spokane map and the scenario as written in Sections 5 and 8; none is observed in a live neighborhood yet. Read it as a structure to argue with. The phrase this drawing replaces is 'polycentric structure' — Marc prefers 'network of nested systems', and wanted both the set view (the nesting) and the network view (the arrows) in one picture.

nodes.label: No one of these systems can hold the student's whole first year. The ME is the connective tissue none of them can be on their own.
nodes.note: Section 8: 'The between-institution project sits in the connective tissue among institutions, small groups, and residents. It exists because a scenario requires an ecosystem to address, and the ecosystem requires work between the parties that none of them would do on their own.'

nodes.label: SCHOOL DISTRICT
nodes.note: The school is one S1 of the district; the district has its own S3 and S5 that decide what the school may commit to.

nodes.label: EXTENDED FAMILY AND KIN
nodes.note: The household is nested in kin relationships that may span continents. Decisions about the child are often made here, not in the household alone.

nodes.label: DIASPORA
nodes.note: The local cultural or religious community is one node of a wider diaspora with its own information, money and trust flows.

nodes.label: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES
nodes.note: Each provider is nested in its own funding, licensing and reporting system. The clinic and the resettlement agency answer to different ones.

nodes.label: TOWN AND COUNTY
nodes.note: The neighborhood is the recursion level the field guide works at. The CHW network is one of the small groups already getting things done there.

nodes.label: SCHOOL
nodes.note: Where enrolment happens and where the first weeks go well or badly. Zero-distance knowledge lives with the school nurse and the teachers.

nodes.label: FAMILY
nodes.note: The household the student is a child in — with its own legal and cultural navigation to do, and often limited English.

nodes.label: CULTURAL COMMUNITY
nodes.note: The community of affiliation where the family will actually seek support first. Its leader's network is where the family is held.

nodes.label: CLINIC
nodes.note: Health services the student and family are clients of. Coordinates through the CHW network.

props.basis: Spokane linkage map #7 — health providers, by implication

nodes.label: RESETTLEMENT AGENCY
nodes.note: Knows the family's arrival context. In Spokane this was World Relief.

nodes.label: NEIGHBORHOOD
nodes.note: The place the family lives — the recursion level the field guide operates on, and where the founded commons is.

nodes.label: CHW NETWORK
nodes.note: Community health workers with existing relationships in the refugee community — the likely navigator role in the ME.

nodes.label: THE STUDENT
nodes.note: Simultaneously a student in the school system, a child in a family, a resident of a neighborhood, a member of a diaspora community, and a client of health and social services. The whole picture is only visible from here.

nodes.label: SOLUTION ME
nodes.note: Forms around the scenario, draws one or two people from each system, charters itself with explicit promises, does the work, and dissolves or continues. Participants come as themselves; their institutions commit separately.

nodes.label: THE SCENARIO
nodes.note: What does the first year in a US school look like for a refugee student, and what would it take across the ecosystem for that year to go well? Lives in the FedWiki repository; outlives every ME that works on it.

edges.label: a parent from an earlier cohort
charters against
edges.note: The charter names the scenario as the object being addressed. The scenario returns to the repository enriched whether the year goes well or badly.
